scope: Audit scope: the local staging working tree and its inspected code, tests and operational documentation. Staging and production are deployed, but this audit does not verify their live revisions or individual feature availability there, except where a feature is recorded in an environment. Unknown availability is intentional, even when implementation is tested.

features.name: Invite-only signup
features.description: Create an account using a valid invite, with server-side invite redemption.
features.notes: Browser invite journeys and atomic-redemption tests exist; production availability is not inferred.

features.name: Email-code sign-in
features.description: Sign in and out using an emailed code rather than a password.

features.name: Email confirmation
features.description: Confirm the email address used to create an account.

features.name: Google sign-in
features.description: Use the configured Google identity provider to access an invited account.
features.notes: google-auth.spec.ts covers signup, sign-in and linking against a local signed OIDC issuer. Live Google consent stays outside automated tests; the owner confirmed a real Google sign-in on staging and production (reported 18 Oct 2026).

features.name: Account recovery
features.description: Regain account access while distinguishing email-code sign-in from a separate recovery process.
features.caveat: Email-code sign-in restores access if you can receive email; a separate process for losing that email account is not provided.
features.notes: Kratos password recovery is explicitly disabled. ADR 0003 replaced it with passwordless sign-in; do not claim a configured recovery flow exists.

features.name: Temporary beta age declaration
features.description: Require new beta members to state that they are 18 or older.
features.notes: Temporary self-declaration, not verified age; under-18 access and voting eligibility remain separate.

features.name: Text posts
features.description: Publish short public posts and delete your own posts.

features.name: Images and descriptions
features.description: Attach up to four processed images to a post, with descriptions for screen readers.
features.notes: Image processing works; abuse-material screening is tracked separately.

features.name: Navigable conversation threads
features.description: Read and expand nested replies with paginated conversation context.

features.name: Likes
features.description: Like a visible post and remove your like.

features.name: Following people
features.description: Follow and unfollow members to shape your Following feed.

features.name: Reposts
features.description: Pass an existing post to your followers without duplicating it in their feed.

features.name: Quote posts
features.description: Add your own words to a shared post while keeping the original in context.

features.name: Sharing and copy link
features.description: Share a post from an in-app popup to WhatsApp, X, Telegram or Facebook, or copy its link.

features.name: External link previews
features.description: Give shared post links descriptive titles, text and available images.

features.name: Links and preview cards in posts
features.description: Web addresses in a post are links, and the first one gets a card with the page's title, text and a picture.
features.notes: Pages are read by the server, which refuses private and local addresses (ADR 0008); readers' browsers never contact the linked site. Only addresses starting http(s):// or www. are linked. Link thumbnails pass the same scanner binding as other uploads.

features.name: GIFs in posts
features.description: Attach a GIF to a post: it plays in the feed, can be paused, and shows its first frame to readers who ask for less motion.
features.notes: Uploaded GIFs only (no search provider); at most 300 frames and 40 million pixels in all, 10 MB. Kept as animated WebP with a still of the first frame, which quoted posts and share previews use.

features.name: Chronological home feeds
features.description: Read Latest and Following in time order, with explanations of Following entries.
features.notes: The local UI says Latest; any For you label is not evidence of personalisation. Reposts use their latest visible entry time (ADR 0007).

features.name: Member profiles
features.description: Edit your photo, name and bio, and browse separate Posts, Replies and Media views.

features.name: Member, community and post search
features.description: Find members, public communities and matching words in posts and replies.

features.name: Public communities
features.description: Browse, join and leave communities, and read or post in their public feeds.

features.name: In-app notifications
features.description: See replies, likes, reposts, quotes, follows and moderation outcomes inside HeyNaija.
features.notes: No push or realtime streaming is implied. Email is a separate feature (email-notifications).

features.name: Block and mute
features.description: Control which accounts and conversations you see using block and mute.

features.name: Reports and moderation
features.description: Report posts or accounts for moderator review under published rules.
features.notes: The permanent moderation log is role-restricted, not a public decision feed.

features.name: Suspension appeals
features.description: Ask moderators to review an account suspension and receive the outcome.

features.name: Moderator tools for profiles and communities
features.description: Moderators can remove a profile photo or clear a name and bio without suspending the account, and site moderators appoint community moderators in the app.
features.notes: Profile reports resolve as remove_avatar or clear_profile; only moderators can, and both are logged. Appointing community moderators is logged and the member is told; site-wide roles are still assigned from the command line (apps/api/src/cli/moderator.ts). Images taken down move out of public view and are kept privately as evidence, so a decision can be undone.

features.name: Action rate limits
features.description: Limit repeated posting, social actions, uploads, reports and other requests.
features.notes: Current in-memory counters reset on restart and are not shared across API instances.

features.name: Pre-publication abuse-material screening
features.description: Screen image uploads before publication through an approved scanning service.
features.caveat: Waiting for PhotoDNA approval; the scanner is written but untried against the real service, and response procedures still need review.
features.notes: NoScanner stays bound until PHOTODNA_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY is set. The PhotoDNA client, GIF frame sampling, fail-closed handling and match reporting have tests against stand-ins; documented Cloudflare edge scanning is a separate second layer.

features.name: Operational abuse response
features.description: Make takedown, preservation, escalation and safety-contact procedures operational.
features.caveat: Reporting, takedown, CDN purge and safety alerts work; counsel's answers, retention decisions and a rehearsed response are still outstanding.
features.notes: Illegal-content reports sort first and are emailed to the safety address; CDN purge needs its Cloudflare token set on each server.

features.name: Deployment and rollback
features.description: Deploy reviewed releases with health checks and a documented rollback path.
features.caveat: Staging and production are deployed; the revision each one runs is not verified.
features.notes: Local HEAD matches the cached origin/staging ref at audit start; no claim that this is the live server revision. The owner reported production running on 18 Oct 2026, when Google sign-in was tested there.

features.name: Backups and tested restoration
features.description: Recover the service and its data from a usable off-site backup.
features.caveat: A local database restore rehearsal is documented; deployed backup checks, media recovery and a current restore rehearsal need confirmation.
features.notes: Staging documentation records a laptop rehearsal but leaves its operational backup/restore checklist unchecked.

features.name: Monitoring and human alerts
features.description: Detect service and backup failures and alert a responsible person.
features.caveat: Health checks, a backup-monitoring hook and external uptime checks of the live sites exist; alerts for errors and failed backups, and who responds, need confirming.
features.notes: The owner set up UptimeRobot monitors on 25 Oct 2026, after the 23 Oct nginx outage: heynaija.ng, its /login and /search, and staging.heynaija.ng, with a public status page. The repository does not record them.

features.name: Constrained mobile performance
features.description: Keep core journeys usable on low-cost phones and slower connections.
features.caveat: Responsive layouts and image resizing exist; measured low-end-device and constrained-network acceptance is still outstanding.

features.name: Core social journeys without JavaScript
features.description: Read feeds, paginate, post and like with JavaScript disabled.
features.caveat: Streamed social pages still depend on JavaScript; the existing no-JavaScript social tests are expected failures.
features.notes: About and Progress are static reading pages and are checked separately from the streamed social feeds.

features.name: Public policies and charter
features.description: Explain current rules, privacy commitments and the proposed governance framework.
features.caveat: The charter, rules and privacy policy apply during the pilot but contain unresolved details; the constitution remains an unadopted proposal.
features.notes: Do not equate publication of drafts with legal adoption or complete operator disclosure.

features.name: Operator and ownership disclosure
features.description: Publish who is responsible for HeyNaija, how it is funded and how to contact them.
features.caveat: Founder-supplied names, operator details, funding information and contact addresses are still needed.

features.name: A working governance feedback channel
features.description: Give readers a real way to comment on governance drafts and see responses.
features.notes: Existing UI says the channel is being prepared; no functional contact is supplied.

features.name: Ideas and problem reports from members
features.description: Suggest a feature or report a problem from inside HeyNaija, add your vote to other ideas, and follow each one from review to release.
features.notes: Built 28 Oct 2026 (ADR 0015). An idea or problem is a post in Building HeyNaija (open to every member, joined or not) whose first line is its title (80 characters), with a kind and a status: under review, planned, in progress, shipped, not now or duplicate. Not now and duplicate need a public reason, and a duplicate's votes move to its original. One vote per member, separate from likes, counted from active members; closed ideas take no new votes. The board (/ideas) lists open, shipped and closed ideas, ideas or problems, by votes or newest; similar ideas show while the title is typed. Problem reports keep the page they came from, the browser and the app version (RELEASE) private to the reporter and the board's moderators. Building HeyNaija's moderators, and site-wide ones, set statuses on the idea's page; each change is on its timeline and notifies the author and voters (idea_status, always on). Reached from the account menu (Ideas and problems; Report a problem, which carries the current page), Building HeyNaija and Progress. The data export (format 10) includes ideas sent and votes. Not built yet: the GitHub App that opens an issue when an idea is planned and brings status back.

features.name: Public source publication
features.description: Publish the source under the existing AGPL licence, and review code ownership and third-party rights.
features.caveat: The source code is public. The review of code ownership and third-party rights, release notes and security disclosure guidance are still to come.
features.notes: Made public on GitHub (github.com/HeyNaija/heynaija) on 29 October 2026, after deploys moved off the self-hosted runners (docs/deployment/staging.md). Confirmed private on 17 October 2026 before that. Constitution Article 12 (v0.3.2) records the remaining ownership and rights review.

features.name: Download your data
features.description: Download your own profile, posts, social choices and account-status records as JSON.
features.notes: Format 10: since format 3 it includes reposts and quoteOf, since format 9 the post pinned to the profile, and since format 10 the ideas you sent (with a problem report's private details) and your votes on the board; restricted person keys and reports about someone stay excluded.

features.name: Guided new-member onboarding
features.description: Help newcomers choose interests, communities and people to follow.
features.notes: New members are sent from the home page to /welcome until they finish or skip it (members.onboarded_at; migration 0019 set it for everyone who joined before). Step 1 chooses communities, step 2 suggests up to 12 people (moderators and recent posters in the chosen communities, then recent posters site-wide; never yourself, suspended members, blocks either way, or people already followed or muted), and finishing joins and follows everything in one transaction through the usual join and follow code, so counts, follow notifications and the shared action rate limit apply; it lands on Following with a nudge to post. Every step, and the whole flow, can be skipped. Communities stand in for interests until topic-following exists; there is no interest or topic picker. No inviter is suggested: invites are admin-created codes. The forms are plain forms, but the page streams like other signed-in pages, so the known no-JavaScript limitation applies. The data export (format 7) includes onboardedAt.

features.name: Basic trending conversations
features.description: Discover recent active conversations using a simple engagement score.
features.notes: Current ranking uses this week’s posts with score 2 × replies + likes, followed by time and ID; it is not state-level analytics or ML personalisation.

features.name: Transparent topic discovery
features.description: Improve Nigerian topic and category discovery with understandable selection rules.
features.notes: Trending topics are hashtags ranked by how many different members used them in live posts and replies in the last 7 days (many uses by one member count once), listed once at least 3 members have; ties go to more posts, then the latest use. Deleted, taken-down and suspended members' posts do not count. The ranking is the same for everyone (no follows, blocks or mutes change it; nothing is picked by hand) and is worked out at most once a minute. Each topic shows its counts and is spelled as most of its uses spell it. The API sends the rules with the topics, and /topics states them in words from those numbers. Shown in the side rail (top 5), on /topics (up to 20), on Search before anything is typed (top 10), and linked from Communities and About. Communities remain the categories; there is no separate category list. No moderator control hides a topic: removing its posts drops it. No topic search yet.

features.name: Clickable hashtags
features.description: Open a topic feed by selecting a hashtag in a post.
features.notes: A # followed by up to 50 letters, digits or underscores, at least one of them a letter, is a hashtag (tone marks typed as separate characters stay in the word); not inside a word (C#), a web address (…#comments) or an HTML entity, and #2027 is a number, not a topic. Each is stored with the post (post_hashtags) under one key for every spelling: composed (NFC) and in lower case, so #EndSARS and #endsars are one topic. In a post it links to /hashtag/<tag as written>, a public page listing live posts and replies with it, newest first, with the usual blocks, mutes and suspensions applied; every spelling's page points search engines at the lower-case one. A search for exactly one #hashtag offers its page. Posts made before hashtags were recorded have no rows, so their #words stay plain text (as with mentions). Trending hashtags are topic-discovery; no topic following or composer suggestions yet.

features.name: Mentions and mention notifications
features.description: Mention a member by handle and notify the person mentioned.
features.notes: Mentions are stored by member ID with their place in the text, so they follow renames; held handles lead to their previous owner. At most 10 members per post are notified; blocked members either way are not, mutes hide the notification, and deleting or removing the post hides it. The composer suggests members after @ and at least one character (GET /v1/search/mentions): people the viewer follows first, by handle or any word of their name, then everyone else by handle start, then by name start, never blocked either way; pages of 10 continue along each index from a cursor (migration 0028), loaded as the list is scrolled or arrowed to its end, and the browser debounces, caches and narrows complete answers locally.

features.name: Pinned profile posts
features.description: Choose a post to keep at the top of your profile.
features.notes: One pin per member (members.pinned_post_id), chosen from the post menu on any of their own live top-level posts; pinning another replaces it. It shows above the first page of their profile's Posts list, marked Pinned, and stays in its place in the list too. It shows only while live and while the reader may see the author (blocks hide it; a mute does not, on the author's own profile). Replies cannot be pinned. The data export (format 9) includes it.

features.name: Pinned community welcome posts
features.description: Keep a welcome post and essential community guidance easy to find.
features.notes: One pin per community (communities.pinned_post_id): any live top-level post in it, its author's or not. Only that community's moderators and site-wide moderators can pin or unpin it, from the post menu wherever the post appears; pinning another replaces it. It shows above the community's Conversations, marked Pinned by the moderators, and only while live and visible to the reader. Pinning is not recorded in the moderation log, and nobody is notified.

features.name: Community photos
features.description: Give communities their own uploaded visual identities.

features.name: Notification preferences
features.description: Choose which activity should create notifications.
features.notes: Settings has one box each for replies, mentions, likes, reposts, quotes and follows; all are on until turned off, and only what is off is stored (notification_opt_outs). A database check keeps moderation and account notices out, so they are always sent. Turning a kind off stops new notifications of that kind and keeps those already received. The kinds decide what notifies a member at all, so they decide what is emailed too; email itself is one switch beside them (email-notifications). The data export (format 7) includes the choices.

features.name: Change your handle or email
features.description: Rename your handle or move your account to a new email address from Settings.
features.notes: A handle someone has is refused at signup and on rename. A handle given up by renaming is held for its owner for 30 days, and its old profile link leads to the new one (ADR 0004). A new email takes over only once a code sent to it is confirmed, after recent sign-in; until then the old one keeps working, and an address another account signs in with is refused before any code is sent.

features.name: Email notifications
features.description: Receive the same notifications by email, grouped into one message, with a one-click way to stop.
features.notes: A background job (BullMQ) looks every minute for members whose oldest waiting notification is five minutes old and who were not emailed in the last 30 minutes, and sends each one email for everything waiting; likes of one post, reposts and follows are rolled into one line. What is emailed is decided when it is sent: nothing the member has read in the app, opted out of, blocked, muted, that was taken down, or that a browser took as a push notification (push-notifications); nothing for suspended members or notifications over a day old; moderation notices are always emailed while email is on, in general words with no post text or reason. One switch in Settings (members.email_notifications), on for members who join from now on and off for everyone who joined before (migration 0021). Every email has a signed one-click unsubscribe link (body and List-Unsubscribe headers, RFC 8058) that turns email off and nothing else. The address is read from Kratos's admin API when sending and is not copied; mail goes through the SMTP account Kratos already uses (Resend, Mailpit locally). Delivery through Resend, and the inbox placement of these emails, have not been checked on staging. The data export (format 7) includes the switch.

features.name: Push activity notifications
features.description: Optionally receive social activity as push notifications outside the app.
features.notes: Web Push with VAPID keys of our own (no Firebase account): Settings has a per-browser button that asks the browser's permission and subscribes it; the service worker (public/sw.js) only shows notifications and opens what they are about. A BullMQ job looks every 10 seconds and pushes what is waiting to each of the member's browsers, in the same words as the email digest: replies, mentions and quotes quote the post briefly, likes, reposts and follows are counted in with ones already pushed and replace them on the device (one tag per post), more than three things at once are one push that says how many, and moderation notices are in general words. What is pushed is decided when it is sent, with the same rules as email: nothing read, opted out of, blocked, muted, taken down, for suspended members, or over ten minutes old. Email waits until the push side has dealt with a notification and leaves out what a browser took (notifications.pushed_at). A browser has one subscription; it moves to whoever turns push on in it, a page load stops one that belongs to another member, and signing out removes it. Subscriptions may only point at Google's, Mozilla's, Apple's or Microsoft's push services. iPhones and iPads get it only from the Home Screen (iOS 16.4+), and Settings says so. The data export (format 8) lists the browsers, without their addresses. The end-to-end tests use a stand-in push service; delivery through the real push services, and how the notifications look on Android, iOS and desktop, have not been checked on staging.

features.name: Accessibility improvements
features.description: Improve keyboard, screen-reader and small-screen access across the product.
features.caveat: Keyboard controls, image descriptions and responsive layouts exist; a full accessibility conformance audit is still needed.

features.name: Light and dark themes
features.description: Follow your device's light or dark setting, or choose one in Settings.
features.notes: The theme is set on <html> before the first paint, so pages do not flash. information.spec.ts checks the device's dark setting is followed and sharing.spec.ts checks the share popup in both themes; the Settings switch itself has no automated test.

features.name: Install HeyNaija as an app
features.description: Add HeyNaija to your home screen or desktop from the welcome steps or Settings, where your browser offers it.
features.notes: The installable web app, not native-apps. Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet offer installation through the Install button; Safari and Firefox do not, and iPhones install from the Share menu. Tests cover the installed app's push offer and iPhone install detection, not the browser's own install prompt.

features.name: Low-data and media controls
features.description: Let members choose how much media loads on limited connections.
features.notes: Upload resizing is implemented; member low-data settings are not. GIFs play unless the device asks for less motion and can be paused. Video is not supported.

features.name: Conversation polls
features.description: Ask an informal question with selectable responses in a post.
features.notes: Ordinary social polls are separate from formal governance ballots.

features.name: More precise reply controls
features.description: Let authors set clearer boundaries around replies to their posts.
features.notes: Nested replies work; per-post reply audience controls are absent.

features.name: Top reply order
features.description: Choose to read a post’s replies with the ones more people answered and liked recently first.
features.notes: Decided 28 Oct 2026 (ADR 0014). A third choice beside Newest (still the default) and Oldest, for the replies to the post in focus; branches stay oldest first. The post author’s replies still come first, then everyone else’s by (2 × members who answered the reply + its likes) / (hours old + 2)^1.5, worked out as of the first page. Nothing depends on who the reader follows or on payment. Offered on posts with up to 2,000 direct replies until wide threads are measured.

features.name: Safeguards for under-18 access
features.description: Prepare approved age assurance, consent, content and contact safeguards before opening younger accounts.
features.caveat: Child-safety decisions, approvals and implementation must precede any change to the temporary adult-only beta.

features.name: Direct messages and message requests
features.description: Support private conversations with blocking, reporting and appropriate contact safeguards.
features.caveat: Message requests, abuse handling, retention and age-appropriate contact safeguards need approval and implementation.
features.notes: No message model or delivery endpoint exists.

features.name: Member lists
features.description: Organise people into lists for easier reading and discovery.

features.name: Saved collections
features.description: Organise privately bookmarked posts into collections.
features.notes: Private bookmarks already work; collections are additional work.

features.name: Follow topics
features.description: Follow a topic as well as people and communities.

features.name: More local discovery
features.description: Discover conversations across more Nigerian states, cities and local communities.
features.caveat: Lagos and Abuja communities exist; wider geographic discovery and location-specific trends do not.

features.name: Community proposals and consultation
features.description: Collect proposals and publish considered responses without implying a binding ballot.
features.caveat: A working consultation channel, responsible reviewers and an agreed process are needed.

features.name: Public governance decision records
features.description: Publish real decisions with reasons and supporting records.
features.notes: Current governance history is an honest empty state; moderator-only logs are not public governance records.

features.name: Optional identity verification
features.description: Offer optional approved-provider identity verification separately from ordinary signup.
features.caveat: Provider approval, privacy and security review, consent and a working integration are prerequisites.
features.notes: The current provider is disabled; startup refuses live verification. No NIN details are being collected.

features.name: Optional verified identity badge
features.description: Let eligible verified members choose whether to display an identity badge.
features.caveat: A live, approved verification process and explicit member choice are required.
features.notes: Groundwork does not activate a green tick; an identity badge would not validate someone’s opinions or posts.

features.name: Verified adult voting membership
features.description: Let every eligible adult legal member voluntarily activate equal participation in the platform governance electorate.
features.caveat: Separate formal legal admission, verified adulthood, identity checks, voluntary activation and approved terms are required; online opt-out preserves legal membership and formal meeting rights.
features.notes: Legal admission is not implemented; preparatory eligibility fails closed. The beta’s self-declared age never establishes verified voting eligibility.

features.name: Member-controlled legal entity
features.description: Proposed nonprofit Incorporated Trustees under CAMA Part F, with three founding trustees on initial three-year terms.
features.caveat: Qualified Nigerian legal review, lawful founding appointments, adopted constitution, CAC incorporation and essential asset transfers remain outstanding.

features.name: Independent ballot assurance
features.description: Review ballot secrecy, eligibility and auditability before formal votes.
features.caveat: A secure ballot design, implementation and independent review are required.
features.notes: No ballot tables or vote endpoints exist; do not build them as part of this task.

features.name: Binding community votes
features.description: Hold lawful member decisions: three trustee seats together at founding-term expiry and every three years thereafter; two representatives annually from readiness.
features.caveat: Activation does not trigger founding trustee re-election. Legal membership, independent secret ballots, formal resolutions and applicable CAC procedures remain required.
features.notes: Binding governance voting cannot be enabled by configuration; an online result alone grants no statutory trustee status.

features.name: Operational public treasury
features.description: Publish actual financial transactions and accountable treasury reports.
features.caveat: An approved operating structure, financial responsibilities and real records are needed.
features.notes: The current UI is a coming-soon preview, not a functioning treasury.

features.name: Account deletion and privacy requests
features.description: Provide a usable route to delete an account and handle privacy requests.
features.caveat: Members can ask for deletion through the contact address, but the time it takes is still to be set and self-service account deletion is absent.
features.notes: Promoted from the initial P2 proposal: a working privacy-rights route is a public-beta prerequisite. The privacy contact is contact@heynaija.ng (apps/web/app/ui/policy-page.tsx); the deletion period is a placeholder on /privacy, and there is no tool for an operator to delete an account.

features.name: Creator analytics
features.description: Offer understandable activity insights without inventing reach or audience metrics.

features.name: Scheduled posts
features.description: Publish a prepared post at a chosen future time.

features.name: Long-form writing
features.description: Support writing beyond the current short-post limit.

features.name: Richer media and video
features.description: Support video with accessible playback and appropriate safety processing.
features.notes: Not before a real upload scanner is bound (upload-scanning): a decision of 18 October 2026, after GIFs and link cards were built.

features.name: Live audio and streaming
features.description: Explore live conversations with moderation and reporting in place.

features.name: Native mobile apps
features.description: Consider native apps if web and installable-app evidence justifies them.
features.notes: A web manifest and icons do not establish a native app or push delivery.

features.name: Creator subscriptions and tips
features.description: Explore creator support with suitable payment and accountability arrangements.

features.name: Community context notes
features.description: Explore crowdsourced context that complements professional moderation.

features.name: Discover: a feed ranked by published rules
features.description: Open Home on Discover: recent posts ranked by rules published on the site, from public activity only, with a reason on every post.
features.notes: Built 28 Oct 2026 (ADR 0014, amended the same day). Discover is the first tab and what Home opens on, for members and signed-out visitors; Latest and Following stay in time order, and Home remembers the tab last chosen (hn_feed cookie). It ranks top-level posts from the last 72 hours: every post starts with 1 point, 2 more for each member who replied in the conversation or quoted it, 1 for each like and repost, 3 more for each person you follow among those who replied, quoted or reposted, 2 if you follow the author, 1 if it is in a community you joined, divided by (hours old + 2)^1.5, with each author’s later posts halved. Your own posts from the last hour come first, unranked. Who liked a post is not public, so likes count only as totals. Posts with open reports from two or more members, or one from the image scanner, wait out of it, and it ends after 100 posts. Pages are ranked as of the moment it was opened, kept in the address (at=). Visitors get the points that are the same for everyone, worked out once a minute and shared. It runs in the API and stores nothing about reading; the rules are sent with every page and shown on /about/discover. Not yet measured on the 20,000-member load-test seed (k6 journeys include it). The charter, privacy policy, About and draft constitution v0.3.1 say what it uses. No learned model.

features.name: Federation and interoperability
features.description: Explore connections to other networks beyond the existing personal data export.
features.notes: Data export exists; federation and protocol interoperability remain Phase 1 non-goals.

features.name: Private bookmarks
features.description: Save visible posts to a bookmark list that only you can read.
